title: Real signage in a generated shot
one_liner: Keep the model performance and the photograph lettering in the same frame.
when: Any generated shot where real text, a logo or a sign has to be legible and correctly spelled. A video model writing text produces confident nonsense, and no seed fixes it - it is not a sampling problem.
how: Matte the characters with BiRefNet (14_birefnet_matte.json), frame by frame. A threshold matte is not good enough to carry a whole frame; that is a rotoscoping job and this is the rotoscoping tool.
DISCARD the model background rather than blending with it. Blending double-exposes, because the model REDRAWS the building rather than moving it.

cv2.findTransformECC, MOTION_AFFINE, with the characters masked OUT of the fit, gives the camera move. Crop each frame background fresh from the full-resolution plate so a push-in gains detail instead of losing it.
If the camera goes somewhere the photograph cannot follow - through a door - hand over to the model own render on a ramp.

knobs.HANDOVER: the scale range over which the plate gives way (1.55 to 1.95)
knobs.plate: which photograph the background is cropped from

gotcha: MOTION_EUCLIDEAN is RIGID - rotation and translation only, no scale. It reported a 0% zoom on a shot that is nothing but a zoom, and buried the error in a 533px pan. Use MOTION_AFFINE.
